pr_title: Fix error where strings were being tracked on IgnoreCycles
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51837

We were currently pushing strings to the stack of references because we were only filtering types that were value types in .NET (`Converter.IsValueType`). This PR adds filtering of types that have `ConverterStrategy != ConverterStrategy.Value` since those can be considered as primitive types in JSON cannot cause a loop. 

Keep in mind that `JsonConverter<object>` also defines `ConverterStrategy` as `ConverterStrategy.Value` therefore I have to special case it.

issue_context.title: ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles not handling duplicate strings properly
comments: JSON team - may want to investigate this behavior for other primitives that have reference equality, such as if a single instance of a boxed integer appears in multiple places.

review_comments: Is the `CanBePolymorphic` check necessary? I believe polymorphic converters can neither be value types or have a `Value` converter strategy.
`ObjectConverter` does have a `Value` converter strategy; that's why I added the `CanBePolymorphic` check, in order to also check for circularity in boxed types.
Got it thanks. I think I was conflating `ObjectConverter` with `ObjectDefaultConverter` which are apparently different.
Why does this hold? IIRC `JsonConverter<object>` can be polymorphic and has `ConverterStrategy.Object`.

Only `JsonObjectConverter<T>` uses `ConverterStrategy.Object`. Any other converter that inherits from JsonConverter<T> uses Value strategy e.g: our internal `ObjectConverter` and for those we don't want to push the reference into the stack here until the value gets unboxed.
How does this work with custom (user) converters (also `ConverterStrategy.Value` and the instance could be a non-primitive)? Do we need to also check `IsInternalConverter`?

Based on local testing, I think we should not push to the stack when the type has a custom converter under the principle that the user should take care of serialization him/herself and because `Preserve` doesn't preserve objects with custom converters.

>Do we need to also check `IsInternalConverter`?

Doesn't `ConverterStrategy != ConverterStrategy.Value` suffice for guarding against custom (user) converters? 
If so, I can add the IsInternalConverter check as an assert.

FWIW: Prior to this change, objects that used an internal converter were failing in the same fashion as the string case reported in the linked issue. 
I added a couple of test cases to cover said scenario (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/52253/commits/a97c9ea8d8175a0c55e0ab91c4481c71c752d011).
